source.name: VocabBuilder starter set (Ukrainian)
source.notes: Hand-written by an AI assistant (Claude) as a small starter set for VocabBuilder. Not corpus-derived: curatedOrder is a teaching order, not a frequency rank. Review and edit freely.

examples.translation: Good afternoon! How can I help you?

examples.text: Добрий день, у вас є вільний столик?
examples.display: До́брий день, у вас є ві́льний сто́лик?
examples.translation: Hello, do you have a free table?

grammar.notes: The standard polite greeting during the day. Informal: приві́т.

examples.translation: Hi! How are you doing?
Hi, I'm home already.

expressions.translation: to say hi (to someone), to send regards

grammar.notes: Informal: for friends, family and anyone you call ти.

examples.translation: Thank you very much for your help.
Thank you for coming.

grammar.notes: Literally 'I thank'. Thank someone with the dative: Дя́кую вам! For something: за + accusative (дя́кую за допомо́гу).

senses.note: The reply to дя́кую; also said when handing something over.

examples.translation: Could I have the bill, please?
Please close the window.
"Thank you!" "You're welcome."
Yes, I speak a little Ukrainian.
Yes, of course, I'll help.

grammar.notes: Also an adverb 'so, like this': Роби́ так.

examples.translation: No, thanks, I don't want any.
No, that's not my phone.

grammar.notes: 'There is no / I don't have' is нема́є + genitive: У мене́ нема́є ча́су.

examples.translation: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
Sorry, I didn't know.

grammar.notes: Polite form for ви; to a friend: ви́бач. перепрошу́ю is another common 'excuse me'.

examples.translation: What do you want for dinner?
What are you talking about?

grammar.notes: Also a conjunction 'that': Я зна́ю, що він удо́ма.

examples.translation: Excuse me, where's the restroom?
Where do you live now?

grammar.notes: Location only. For direction ('where to') use куди́: Куди́ ти йдеш?

examples.translation: Excuse me, what's your name?
How do you say this in Ukrainian?

expressions.translation: How are you? / How's it going?

examples.text: Брат і сестра живуть у Львові.
examples.display: Брат і сестра́ живу́ть у Льво́ві.
examples.translation: My brother and sister live in Lviv.
Borscht and varenyky are very tasty.

grammar.notes: For smooth sound, й is used after a vowel before a consonant (ма́ма й та́то); та is a common alternative (ма́ма та та́то).

examples.text: Я хочу піти, але не маю часу.
examples.display: Я хо́чу піти́, але́ не ма́ю ча́су.
examples.translation: I want to go, but I don't have time.
It's expensive here, but very tasty.
I was at home all evening.

examples.text: Ти будеш на вечірці в суботу?
examples.display: Ти бу́деш на вечі́рці в субо́ту?
examples.translation: Will you be at the party on Saturday?

grammar.notes: Present tense є is the same for all persons and is usually left out: Я вдо́ма 'I'm at home'. Past: був, була́, було́, були́.

examples.translation: I want a cup of coffee.
What would you like to order?

grammar.notes: Stress on the stem throughout the present: хо́чу, хо́чеш, хо́чемо, хо́чуть.

senses.note: Perfective partner in the sense 'to say, to tell': сказа́ти.

examples.translation: Please speak slowly.
My mom speaks very fast.

grammar.notes: Stress moves to the stem after the 1st person singular: говорю́, but гово́риш, гово́рять. 'To speak a language' is usually розмовля́ти: Ви розмовля́єте англі́йською?

examples.text: Я не розумію, повторіть, будь ласка.
examples.display: Я не розумі́ю, повторі́ть, будь ла́ска.
examples.translation: I don't understand, could you repeat that, please?
Do you understand what he's saying?

grammar.notes: Perfective: зрозумі́ти (зрозумі́ю, зрозумі́в).

examples.text: Я не знаю, де він живе.
examples.display: Я не зна́ю, де він живе́.
examples.translation: I don't know where he lives.
Do you know his phone number?

grammar.notes: No perfective partner in this sense; дізна́тися means 'to find out'.

examples.translation: Can you help me?
I can't today, sorry.

grammar.notes: г/ж alternation: мо́жу, мо́жеш… мо́жуть; past міг, могла́, могли́.

examples.translation: He's a very kind person.
There are too many people here today.

grammar.notes: Feminine even when it refers to a man: Він до́бра люди́на. Plural: лю́ди, люде́й.

examples.translation: Could I have a glass of water, please?

examples.text: Я завжди беру з собою воду.
examples.display: Я завжди́ беру́ з собо́ю во́ду.
examples.translation: I always take water with me.

grammar.notes: Stress moves to the stem in the accusative singular and in the plural: во́ду, во́ди (genitive singular води́).

examples.translation: That's really good news!
She has a very kind heart.

grammar.notes: Also 'kind' (of people). Comparative: кра́щий 'better'. до́бре = well, OK.

examples.translation: I'm at work right now.
Wait, I'll be right there.
What day of the week is it today?
Today I'm working from home.
Excuse me, is this seat free?
I've been living here for a year.

grammar.notes: Location 'here'. For direction ('to here') use сюди́: Іди́ сюди́!

examples.translation: I really like Kyiv.
Nice to meet you, my name is Oleg.

examples.text: Я живу в Києві вже два роки.
examples.display: Я живу́ в Ки́єві вже два ро́ки.
examples.translation: I've been living in Kyiv for two years.
Where does your family live?

grammar.notes: Stress on the ending: живу́, живе́ш, живемо́. Past: жив, жила́, жили́.

examples.translation: What are you doing tonight?
We always do this together.

grammar.notes: б → бл in the 1st person singular and 3rd person plural: роблю́, ро́блять. Stress moves to the stem after роблю́.

examples.text: Скажіть, будь ласка, скільки це коштує?
examples.display: Скажі́ть, будь ла́ска, скі́льки це ко́штує?
examples.translation: Excuse me, how much does this cost?
What did he tell you yesterday?

grammar.notes: Perfective, so no present tense: скажу́ = 'I'll say'. з → ж: скажу́, ска́жеш. Скажі́ть, будь ла́ска… is a polite way to start a question.

examples.translation: Our house is very old.
There's a park near our house.

grammar.notes: і → о in other forms: дім → до́му. вдо́ма = at home, додо́му = (to) home. For a building, буди́нок is more common.

examples.translation: I'm still at work.
He's looking for a new job.

grammar.notes: на робо́ту = to work; на робо́ті = at work.

examples.translation: This is my old friend.

examples.text: У суботу я зустрічаюся з друзями.
examples.display: У субо́ту я зустріча́юся з дру́зями.
examples.translation: On Saturday I'm meeting up with friends.

grammar.notes: Vocative (when addressing someone): дру́же! Plural: дру́зі, дру́зів.

examples.translation: I have a big family.
I miss my family.

grammar.notes: Synonym: сім’я́. сумува́ти за + instrumental = to miss.

examples.translation: I often call my mom.
Mom, I'm home!

grammar.notes: Vocative when addressing her: ма́мо! дзвони́ти + dative: дзвоню́ ма́мі.

examples.translation: I don't have time.
How long does the trip take?

grammar.notes: To ask the time, say Котра́ годи́на? 'What time is it?'

examples.text: Я працюю п’ять днів на тиждень.
examples.display: Я працю́ю п’ять днів на ти́ждень.
examples.translation: I work five days a week.
It was a very long day.

grammar.notes: The е drops out in other forms: дня, дні, днів.

examples.translation: See you tomorrow at nine in the morning.
Tomorrow is my day off.

senses.note: One direction, on foot, at a particular time.

examples.translation: I'm already heading home.
Where are you going so early?

grammar.notes: After a consonant the forms with і- are used: іти́, іду́, іде́ш (він іде́). For habitual or round trips use ходи́ти; by vehicle use ї́хати.

senses.note: One direction, by car, bus, train etc.

examples.translation: Tomorrow we're going to Kyiv.
I'm taking the bus to work.

grammar.notes: For habitual or round trips use ї́здити. Destination: до + genitive (до Ки́єва); transport in the instrumental (авто́бусом, по́тягом).

examples.translation: I don't eat meat.
What do you eat for breakfast?

grammar.notes: Irregular: їм, їси́, їсть, їмо́, їсте́, їдя́ть; past їв, ї́ла.

examples.translation: She drinks tea with milk.
I don't drink coffee in the evening.

grammar.notes: Apostrophe after п in the present: п’ю, п’єш, п’є, п’ємо́, п’єте́, п’ють.

examples.translation: I'll buy bread and milk.
Where did you buy this jacket?

grammar.notes: Perfective; imperfective купува́ти (купу́ю). п → пл: куплю́, ку́плять; stress moves to the stem after куплю́.

examples.translation: I'll do it tomorrow.
Have you ordered yet?

grammar.notes: Perfective of роби́ти: зроблю́ = 'I will do (and finish)'.

examples.text: Купи, будь ласка, хліб і сир.
examples.display: Купи́, будь ла́ска, хліб і сир.
examples.translation: Please buy some bread and cheese.
We're out of bread.
Would you like some tea with lemon?
We drink tea in the kitchen.
Let's have a coffee after work.
Your coffee is already cold.

grammar.notes: Feminine and fully declined: ка́ва, ка́ви, ка́ву, ка́вою.

examples.text: Я йду до магазину по хліб.
examples.display: Я йду до магази́ну по хліб.
examples.translation: I'm going to the shop for bread.
Everything is cheaper in this shop.

grammar.notes: Genitive in -у: магази́ну. по + accusative = to go and get: по хліб. A small shop is also called крамни́ця.

examples.text: У мене немає з собою грошей.
examples.display: У мене́ нема́є з собо́ю гро́шей.
examples.translation: I don't have any money on me.
This money is for groceries.

grammar.notes: Plural only (no gender): ці гро́ші 'this money'. Genitive: гро́шей.

examples.translation: The weather is really nice today.
You have a very beautiful city.

grammar.notes: Very common for 'nice, beautiful'. Comparative: кра́щий 'better, nicer'.

examples.text: У мене погана пам’ять на імена.
examples.display: У мене́ пога́на па́м’ять на імена́.
examples.translation: I have a bad memory for names.
I think it's a bad idea.

grammar.notes: Comparative: гі́рший 'worse'. Adverb: пога́но (Мені́ пога́но 'I feel unwell').

examples.translation: Kyiv is a very big city.
They live in a big house.

grammar.notes: Comparative: бі́льший 'bigger'.

examples.text: У нас маленька квартира в центрі.
examples.display: У нас мале́нька кварти́ра в це́нтрі.
examples.translation: We have a small apartment in the center.
My son is still little.

grammar.notes: Comparative: ме́нший 'smaller'.

examples.translation: This is my new phone.
Happy New Year to you!

grammar.notes: Stress on the ending in all forms: нови́й, нова́, нове́, нові́.

senses.note: In greetings and letters: Дорогі́ дру́зі!

examples.translation: This restaurant is too expensive.
Dear friends, happy holidays!

grammar.notes: Stress on the ending: дороги́й, дорога́. Comparative: доро́жчий. Adverb: до́рого.

examples.translation: The borscht here is really good.
Mom makes really tasty varenyky.

grammar.notes: Stress on the ending: смачни́й, смачна́. Adverb: сма́чно.

examples.translation: I like this city.
We live in the city center.

grammar.notes: Stress moves to the ending in the nominative plural: міста́ (singular мі́сто, мі́ста). Locative: у мі́сті.

examples.translation: What street do you live on?
Cross to the other side of the street.

grammar.notes: на ву́лиці = on the street. 'Outside, outdoors' is usually надво́рі: Надво́рі хо́лодно.

examples.translation: I'll call you in a week.
I'm very busy this week.

grammar.notes: The е drops out: ти́ждень → ти́жня. Don't confuse with неді́ля 'Sunday'.

examples.translation: I left my phone at home.
He's on the phone right now.

grammar.notes: 'To talk on the phone' is розмовля́ти телефо́ном (instrumental). Genitive in -у: телефо́ну.

examples.translation: I'm learning Ukrainian.
How many languages do you know?

grammar.notes: 'Tongue' (the body part) is язи́к. 'In Ukrainian' is украї́нською (мо́вою).

examples.translation: They have two children.
Our child is already asleep.

grammar.notes: Feminine: на́ша дити́на. Plural: ді́ти, діте́й.

examples.translation: Wash your hands before eating.
I broke my arm as a child.

grammar.notes: Stress moves to the stem in the accusative singular and nominative plural: ру́ку, ру́ки (genitive singular руки́).

examples.translation: I have a headache.
I've just washed my hair.

grammar.notes: Stress moves to the stem in the accusative: го́лову. ми́ти го́лову = to wash one's hair.

examples.translation: I need to see a doctor.
You need to call a doctor.

grammar.notes: Animate: accusative = genitive (ви́кликати лі́каря). Plural stress on the ending: лікарі́.

examples.text: Я вже купив квиток на потяг.
examples.display: Я вже купи́в квито́к на по́тяг.
examples.translation: I've already bought a train ticket.
Two tickets, please.

grammar.notes: The о drops out: квито́к → квитка́. After 2–4 Ukrainian uses the nominative plural: два квитки́.
